page.title: Alerts
page.description: Alert profiles, rules and the OBS Browser Source queue - built on the same normalized Engagement Event Bus as Chat and Automation.

profiles.deleteConfirmMessage: Deleting "{{name}}" removes every rule that belongs to it and immediately invalidates its Browser Source URL. This cannot be undone.
profiles.rotateConfirmMessage: The current URL for "{{name}}" will stop working immediately. Update the Browser Source in OBS with the new URL afterward.

fields.name: Name
fields.enabledHint: A disabled profile accepts no new alerts and its Browser Source shows nothing.
fields.languageHint: Language used for this profile's own built-in text (such as the event-type name) - never inferred from who last edited it.
fields.maxQueueItemsHint: 1-500. When full, a new alert only displaces the current lowest-priority queued one.
fields.maximumQueueAgeSecondsHint: 5-3600. A queued alert older than this is skipped rather than played late.

queue.title: Queue
queue.clearConfirmMessage: Every queued (not yet playing) alert for this profile is removed. The alert currently playing, if any, is not affected.
queue.replayUnavailable: No previous alert to replay yet.
queue.inputGapWarning: The Event Bus connection was briefly lost and later reconnected - some events during that window may not have been matched.

rules.title: Rules
rules.empty: No alert rules yet for this profile.
rules.deleteConfirmMessage: Deleting "{{name}}" stops it from matching any further event immediately.
rules.testSentNotice: A real, synthetic test alert was sent through the real queue - watch the Browser Source to see it.
rules.overlapWarning: This rule's quantity range overlaps another enabled rule for the same event type ({{other}}) - one real event may trigger both.

fields.name: Name
fields.priorityHint: 0-100. Higher plays first among queued alerts; never interrupts one already playing.
fields.quantityHint: Leave blank for unbounded on that side. Both bounds are inclusive.
fields.providersHint: Twitch is currently the only supported provider, so this makes little difference today - it exists so a rule can be pinned to Twitch specifically once another provider is added, rather than matching every future one by default.
fields.allowGroupingHint: Only alerts still waiting in the queue are ever merged - the alert currently visible is never changed into a group. Merging never extends how long the group can wait before it expires, and only genuinely matching real events from the same person merge together.
fields.groupingHidesMessageHint: Grouping is only safe when no single member's message is shown, since a merged alert can no longer point to one specific message - "Show message" has been turned off for you.
fields.groupWindowMsHint: 1000-30000 milliseconds, counted from the first alert in the group. A later match after the window closes starts a new group instead of joining this one.
fields.groupingTemplateUnsafe: This template still references the message placeholder, which is unsafe once grouping is enabled - remove it or turn grouping off.
fields.interruptEnabledHint: When a real event matches this rule, it immediately replaces whatever is currently playing, but only if that alert's own priority is strictly lower and it allows itself to be interrupted. Equal priority never interrupts. Disabled while the queue is paused.
fields.interruptible: Allow this alert to be interrupted
fields.interruptibleHint: Lets a later, higher-priority, interruption-enabled alert replace this one while it is playing. An interrupted alert is never resumed automatically - use Replay Previous to show it again.

rules.groupingUnavailableHint: No safe way to group this event type exists - merging different people's events, or aggregating a value that would become misleading, is never attempted.
rules.roleUnavailableHint: No currently supported event type reports viewer roles - this field is reserved for a future connector.
